materialFinancialSemantics: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory; zero native value required.

Ethereum coveUSD BasketToken 0xeea3edc017877c603e2f332fc1828a46432cdf96 is an EIP1167 minimal clone of 0xaafa26aa70e7e1119b32fdb2dfc07f8e3eba0987, confirmed by current explorer and observed clone bytecode. Implementation runtime/creation source grades are match, not exact_match; root Sourcify record is absent. This is Coves own basket capital product, not a Yearn curator-labeled vault or its legacy Boosties liquid locker.

Observed base asset is Ethereum USDC 0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48 (6 decimals); coveUSD shares use 18 decimals. requestDeposit transfers owner assets into token custody; requestRedeem escrows owner coveUSD. Owners/controllers normally should be the caller; existing operator or share allowance can authorize other-owned balances. None of these methods installs an operator, approval, permit or signature authority.

Not synchronous generic ERC4626: request methods fund an epoch first; deposit/mint only claim already-fulfilled deposit shares, and redeem/withdraw only claim already-fulfilled USDC redemptions. Claims require the full current controllers amount; deposit/mint and withdraw/redeem are paired alternative claim forms, not repeatable independent outputs. Allocation floors proportionally across epoch totals; no caller minimum output, deadline or price limit is provided.

BasketManager settles pending epochs during rebalancing, transfers successful deposit assets into shared strategy custody and supplies USDC for successful redemption. Rates and settlement timing depend on rebalance execution, oracles, strategy markets and counterparties; typical 24-hour docs timing is not a deadline. New requests can be blocked by outstanding pending/claimable claims or paused registered assets.

cancelDepositRequest/cancelRedeemRequest only cancel the callers own still-current pending epoch, returning USDC/coveUSD respectively. Once the manager advances that epoch these cancellations are unavailable. claimFallbackAssets returns a failed ordinary deposit epochs full USDC; claimFallbackShares returns failed ordinary redemption epochs full escrowed shares, only after manager marks zero fulfillment. These are ordinary request-failure branches, not hacked/recovery-only product admission.

proRataRedeem burns owned or previously authorized shares and returns a floor-rounded basket of current manager-held tokens, not guaranteed USDC or their underlying redemptions. It is blocked while the basket rebalances and by manager pause/role constraints. It harvests management-fee dilution before computing the basket payout and has no minimum basket-output bounds.

Fees are configurable: BasketToken management fee is annual BPS share dilution to fee collector, capped in source at 3000 BPS, using fee*time/((10000-fee)*365 days) on supply excluding collector holdings. Rebalance internal-trade fees, swap costs, strategy fees and price/oracle losses may affect NAV; no current fee-rate or principal/yield guarantee is asserted.

Observed BasketManager 0x716c39658ba56ce34bdecdc1426e8768e61912f8 and AssetRegistry 0xd57950e8e9111ca49b1a041ed6c53a1355e317c7 match primary directory. Their current runtime/library/governance, strategy, oracle and token dependencies are not independently attested here. Full compiled dependency sources are retained only as source context. Existing ERC20 token plugins may receive transfer callbacks; plugin installation/removal, multicall, permit, admin and rebalance execution functions are excluded.

devdoc.details: Considerations for Integrators: When users call `requestDeposit` or `requestRedeem`, the system ensures that the controller does not have any pending or claimable deposits or redeems from the controller's `lastDepositRequestId`. This behavior allows for a potential griefing attack: an attacker can call `requestDeposit` or `requestRedeem` with a minimal dust amount and specify the target controller address. As a result, the target controller would then be unable to make legitimate `requestDeposit` or `requestRedeem` requests until they first claim the pending request. RECOMMENDATION FOR INTEGRATORS: When integrating `BasketToken` into other contracts, always check for any pending or claimable tokens before requesting a deposit or redeem. This ensures that any pending deposits or redeems are resolved, preventing such griefing attacks.

devdoc.details: Considerations for Integrators: When users call `requestDeposit` or `requestRedeem`, the system ensures that the controller does not have any pending or claimable deposits or redeems from the controller's `lastDepositRequestId`. This behavior allows for a potential griefing attack: an attacker can call `requestDeposit` or `requestRedeem` with a minimal dust amount and specify the target controller address. As a result, the target controller would then be unable to make legitimate `requestDeposit` or `requestRedeem` requests until they first claim the pending request. RECOMMENDATION FOR INTEGRATORS: When integrating `BasketToken` into other contracts, always check for any pending or claimable tokens before requesting a deposit or redeem. This ensures that any pending deposits or redeems are resolved, preventing such griefing attacks.

devdoc.details: Considerations for Integrators: When users call `requestDeposit` or `requestRedeem`, the system ensures that the controller does not have any pending or claimable deposits or redeems from the controller's `lastDepositRequestId`. This behavior allows for a potential griefing attack: an attacker can call `requestDeposit` or `requestRedeem` with a minimal dust amount and specify the target controller address. As a result, the target controller would then be unable to make legitimate `requestDeposit` or `requestRedeem` requests until they first claim the pending request. RECOMMENDATION FOR INTEGRATORS: When integrating `BasketToken` into other contracts, always check for any pending or claimable tokens before requesting a deposit or redeem. This ensures that any pending deposits or redeems are resolved, preventing such griefing attacks.
